Done. Each monster now attacks independently, and I kept it rules-correct.

## What changed (`static/app.js`)

**Per-monster attack** — every standing monster now has its own **"👹 Strike hero"** button in its row. You trigger only the monsters that are actually in range that round; the rest sit out. After a monster goes, its button dims to **"👹 ✓ attacked"** so you can see who's already acted.

**Armor stays once-per-round.** This was the tricky part — the rulebook says armor is subtracted from the round's *total*, once per round, not per hit. So I added a per-round armor pool that depletes across each monster's strike. Mathematically identical to summing all hits and subtracting armor once, but it works even when attacks are resolved one button at a time. I verified it against the rulebook's own example (3 Goblins, 3A armor → 3 HP lost) and it matches exactly. The combat panel shows **"Armor this round: X/Y left to absorb"** so the mitigation is transparent.

**Round controls** replace the old single "Monsters Attack →" button:
- **"👹 All in range attack"** — convenience that strikes only monsters who haven't gone yet this round (skips the ones you've already resolved).
- **"End round →"** — refreshes the armor pool, advances the round, clears the "attacked" markers.

The pool also resets on new encounters and re-rolls, so a depleted round-1 pool never carries between rooms. Reinforcements added mid-fight can attack the same round (they have no "attacked" marker yet).

Monster specials (poison, chill, etc.) aren't auto-applied — same as before — but each strike's d6 and the special text are surfaced in the log so you can adjudicate triggers.

blocks.text:
Fixed. `castCombatSpell` was rolling and dealing damage but never touching `h.ap`.

## What it does now

- **Deducts AP on cast.** Fixed-cost spells (Magic Missile 1, Frost Bolt 2, Fireball 3, etc.) subtract their `ap` value from your current AP.
- **Spent on hit *or* miss** — AP is deducted before the roll, since casting expends the action either way (per the rules).
- **Blocks unaffordable casts.** If you don't have enough AP it alerts (`Not enough AP for Fireball: need 3, have 1.`) and cancels instead of firing for free.
- **Handles "varies" spells.** Life Drain prompts for how much AP to spend, then heals 1 HP per 2 AP spent on a hit — so the variable spend actually matters.
- **Logs the cost** — each cast line ends with `[−3 AP]` so you can see the drain in the combat log, and the AP bar updates immediately.

blocks.text:
All in place. Here's how monster cards now connect to board tokens:

## How it works

**Pin a monster to the board:** Each monster card in the combat manager has a new **📍 Place** button. Click it, then click any square on the map — that monster's token drops onto the square. The button changes to **📍 on board** once placed; click it again to **move** the token (then click a new square). While placing, the map shows a gold hint banner (*"Placing Goblin A — click a square…"*) with a cancel link, and squares get a dashed highlight.

**Token ↔ card link:** The token shows a short tag that matches the card — the **A/B/C letter** when there are multiples of a type, **👑** for a boss, or the monster's initial for a lone monster. It also shows the monster's **current HP** in the corner and the full label + HP on hover. Bosses get a gold-bordered token.

**Auto-disappear on death — the key part:** Tokens are keyed to each monster's `uid`, but the board only renders tokens for monsters with **HP > 0**. So the moment a monster drops (via attack, spell, or free-form damage — all routes funnel through `killMonster`), its token vanishes on the next render. No separate bookkeeping to get out of sync.

**Bonus — revive works too:** Because the token's position is retained (just hidden while dead), hitting the **↺ revive** button on a slain monster brings its token right back to where it was.

**Edge cases handled:** Re-rolling or clearing the encounter wipes tokens (so recycled uids can't mis-point), generating a new room starts fresh, removing a monster (✕) prunes its token, and only one monster can occupy a square (placing on an occupied square moves the previous one off).

Two small things worth noting:
- The old generic **👹 Monster** paint tool still exists for free-form scribbling. The new linked tokens are separate and more powerful — want me to remove the old paint tool to avoid confusion, or keep both?
- The server wasn't running when I checked, so I couldn't click through it live. The code parses clean and the assets are updated on disk. Want me to launch the app so you can see it, or will you open it yourself?

## How the Archmage's Staff bonus spell now works

**A dedicated, anchored slot.** `h.staffSpell` holds the one spell the staff grants — separate from your base profession slots (which stay capped at `prof.spells`). The staff adds exactly one extra, on top of the base cap.

**Built into the staff.** When the staff is equipped, a bordered **🪄 Archmage's Staff — bonus spell** panel appears under your Spells with a dropdown. Pick any spell-book spell (ones already base-memorized are excluded so you can't double-list), and it becomes castable. Choosing "— none —" clears it. The Spells header also shows `+1 via Archmage's Staff`.

**Anchored to the staff.** `equip()` and `unequip()` both clear `h.staffSpell` the moment the weapon slot stops being the staff — whether you unequip it or swap in another weapon. A log line records it: *"Unequipping the Archmage's Staff removed its bonus spell (Fireball) from memory."* So the bonus spell genuinely lives and dies with the staff.

**The note on the spell.** In the spell-book list, the staff-provided spell shows a **🪄** icon (instead of the memorize checkbox, so it can't be double-counted) and a **"via Archmage's Staff"** tag next to its name — making clear where it's coming from.

**Fully castable.** `memorizedSpells(h)` returns base memorized + the staff spell, and the combat manager's per-monster ✦ buttons and the spell-list Cast buttons both use it — so the bonus spell works in combat exactly like a memorized one, deducting AP through the same path.

One edge worth noting: if you base-memorize 3 (Wizard), set the staff bonus to a 4th, then unequip the staff, you cleanly drop back to your 3 — no over-cap state, no manual cleanup needed. That's the payoff of making it a separate anchored slot rather than a shared +1.

blocks.text:
Fixed at the root. The master list of all 15 spells was already coded into the Spells tab, but it never rendered because of a bug in the core `el()` helper.

## What was actually wrong

`apLabel(3)` returns the **number** `3` for a numeric AP cost, and `refSpells` passed it straight into a table cell: `el("td", {...}, apLabel(s.ap))`. The old `el()` only converted *strings* to text nodes and passed everything else to `appendChild()` directly — and `appendChild(3)` throws in the browser. So the spell-list table died on its first row (Blink, AP 3), aborting the function right after the two rules sections had already rendered. That's why you saw the explanatory text but no list — and it's the same reason the tab looked "empty" back at the very start.

## The fix

One line in `el()` — coerce any non-node child (numbers included) to a text node instead of throwing:

```js
n.appendChild(typeof kid === "object" ? kid : document.createTextNode(String(kid)));
```

Verified against the real spell data: the table now renders **all 15 spells** (16 rows with the header) — Blink, Enchant Weapon, Enfeeble, Enwizen, Fear, Fireball, Frost Bolt, Haste, Knock, Life Drain, Magic Missile, Quicken, Shocking Grasp, Strengthen, Tangle — each with AP, Combat (R/D/H), and Effect.

**Bonus:** the Rulebook's **Professions** tab had the identical bug (its ability tables also use `apLabel(a.ap)` as a direct cell child), so those ability tables were silently failing too. They render now as well.

The Spells tab now shows: *How spellcasting works* → *What the values mean* → the full **Spell list** table.

One heads-up: the desktop app runs in a WKWebView that caches `app.js` aggressively. If the list still doesn't show after this, fully quit and relaunch the Pocket Dungeon app (not just close the window) to force a fresh load. Want me to launch it now so we can confirm the table's there?

blocks.text:
No — 2 is correct. Those are two different numbers, and it's a common point of confusion:

- **Starting spells = 2.** Per the trappings rule: a spellcaster begins with *"either one weapon or (for spellcasters) two spells."* So your Wizard correctly started knowing **2 spells** in his spell book (Tangle and Magic Missile).
- **`Up to 3 spells memorized` = the cap, not your repertoire.** The Wizard's "3" is the *maximum he can have memorized at once* — it's a ceiling, not how many he knows. He only fills it as he learns more spells.

So your Wizard knows 2, and has room to memorize a 3rd (and the Archmage's Staff bumps the cap to 4) — but he can't memorize spells he doesn't know yet.

**How he learns more:** spells get added to his spell book through play, not at creation:
- **Spell Scroll** (treasure) — adds any one spell from the Spells table to your book.
- **Spell book page** (magic item) — adds any 2 spells, then crumbles.
- **Library** special room — roll 3 times on the Scroll table.

Once he picks up a 3rd spell, you'll be able to memorize all three; a 4th becomes castable through the staff's bonus slot.

This is also exactly why the staff looked useless earlier — he had 2 known spells against a base cap of 3, so there was nothing extra to slot until he learns more (which is why I had the staff channel from the full spell list). Everything's working as the rules intend — no bug here. Want me to drop a quick "Spells known vs. memorize cap" note into the character sheet or the Spells rulebook tab so this is clear at a glance?

Each ability is an expandable row showing its **name**, **AP cost**, and (when expanded) its full **effect text** — and an action button:

## Selling is a *between-dungeons* activity

Per the rulebook: *"A hero who completes a dungeon… may sell unwanted trappings for gold, and may upgrade items with gold and Bonus Rating."* Selling happens in the "town"/shop phase **between dungeons**, not mid-run.

In the app:
- **During an active dungeon** (where you are now, fighting Kobolds) your inventory items only offer equip / use / learn / drop — no sell. That's intentional.
- **After you complete a dungeon** (defeat the boss in room 30), the Dungeon panel turns into a **"Between Dungeons"** screen with a **"Sell trappings"** list — every item gets a **sell** button, and the gold lands in your hero's Gold stat. From there you descend to the next tier.

The payouts follow the rules:
- **Weapon** = R + D + H (+5 exotic)
- **Armor/shield** = 3 × Armor value
- **Potion** 1g · **Scroll** 3g · **Magic trinket** ~12g
- Spells in your book can't be sold (they're not items).

text: How do I deal with trapped chests as a Wizard?

blocks.text:
Short version: as a Wizard, you can't disarm it — you just open it and eat the **1 HP**. Here's the full picture.

## Trapped chests in Pocket Dungeon

A chest rolls one status: **Unlocked**, **Locked**, or **Trapped** (they're mutually exclusive, not stacked).

- **Trapped** → opening it deals **1 HP that cannot be mitigated** — armor, shields, and damage-blocking abilities don't reduce it. That 1 HP is simply the price of looting it.
- The only way to *avoid* the trap is the Thief's **Disarm Trap** ability (roll d6 +1 per 3 Agility, removes the trap on 5+). **Wizards have no trap-disarm** — it's not in your abilities (Dark Rituals, Spell Recall, Empower, Heighten, the Ethereal trio) and there's no disarm spell in the Spells table.

So your options as a Wizard are just: **open it and take the 1 HP, or leave it unopened** (no loot, no damage).

## Don't confuse it with a Locked chest

- **Locked** chests *can* be handled by a Wizard — the **Knock** spell ("Unlock a door or chest") or a **Skeleton Key** opens them. (You don't currently know Knock — only Tangle and Magic Missile — but you could learn it from a Spell Scroll.)
- **Trapped** is different: there's no lock to pick, just the guaranteed 1 HP hit.

## In the app

When you open a chest marked **⚠ Trapped**, it automatically deducts 1 HP (logged as *"Trapped chest! −1 HP (cannot be mitigated)"*) and rolls your treasure. Since your Wizard has a low HP pool (base 6), just be mindful of your current HP before opening one — if you're low, heal first (Potion of Healing, Healing Font, etc.). But 1 HP for loot is almost always worth it.

So you're not missing a mechanic — taking the small unavoidable hit *is* how a Wizard deals with trapped chests. Want me to add an on-screen note about this to the chest-opening flow, or a confirm prompt for trapped chests (like the one Locked chests get) so you don't trigger one by accident?

## The rules: monsters stack
Only the squares **orthogonally adjacent to your hero** are limited to one monster each. **Any non-adjacent square holds any number** of monsters. Only the adjacent ones can attack each round; the stacked ones move up as adjacent slots free (kills, repositioning). Everything fits — it just stacks.

## The fix: tokens now stack on the board
My monster-token feature was wrongly forcing one token per square (that's why you couldn't place all four). Now:
- **Multiple monster tokens can share a square.** Drop as many as you want on one cell.
- A stacked square shows **"×N"** with a gold border, and **hovering lists every monster and its HP** (e.g. "Kobolds B 3/3, Kobolds C 3/3").

blocks.text:
Yes — every non-boss room is rolled for it. Looking at the generation code (`generateRoom`), here's exactly how it works:

```js
if (!isBossRoom) {
  const tr = tableLookup(G.dungen.treasure, roll(8));   // d8, every room
  if (tr === "SR") { special = G.specialRooms.table[roll(6) - 1]; ... }
  else chestCount = tr;
}
```

The special-room check **is** the treasure roll — it's not a separate roll. Each room rolls one **d8** on the Treasure table:

| d8 | Result |
|----|--------|
| 1–2 | no treasure |
| 3–5 | 1 chest |
| 6–7 | 2 chests |
| **8** | **Special Room** (and no chests that room) |

So a roll of exactly **8 → Special Room**, which is a **1-in-8 (12.5%) chance per room**. Then a d6 picks which one: Healing Font, Altar of Blessing, Armory, Alchemy Lab, Library, or Arcane Forge.

This is RAW-correct (the rulebook: *"Roll # Treasure for chests; an 'SR' result is a Special Room"*). The only room that **doesn't** get rolled is the **boss room (room 30)** — it's always the boss, no treasure or special room.

So it's working as intended — you just haven't hit one yet. You're on room 6, and at 12.5% per room there was only about a ~55% chance you'd have seen one by now, so a dry streak is totally normal. Your odds of hitting at least one over a full 29-room dungeon are ~98%, so they'll show up.

Built and migrated. Here's the new persistent chest system:

## How it works now
Chests are now **dungeon-level objects** (`d.chests`), not tied to a room — so they survive moving on and you can interact with them from anywhere.

**The Chests panel** (in the Dungeon panel) lists every chest in the dungeon — its status (📦/🔒/⚠/📭 opened), which room it's from, and whether it's on the board. Each has three buttons:
- **Open** — applies the effect from anywhere (Locked → confirm; Trapped → confirms, then −1 HP; rolls treasure). Disappears once opened.
- **📍 Place / Move** — exactly like monster tokens: click it, then click a board square to drop the chest token (click its square again to lift it off).
- **✕** — remove the chest.

**On the board:** placed chests render as 📦 tokens (with 🔒/⚠ badges; opened ones show 📭, dimmed). They share squares freely with monsters/hero (chests don't block).

**The panel shows even after a room is finished**, so you can generate new rooms and still go back and open old chests — true backtracking.

I also retired the old cosmetic "Chest 📦" paint tool (the palette is now Floor · Wall · Door · Hero · Erase) since functional chest tokens replace it.

- 📭 **Unlocked · room 7** — already opened (your Scroll of Healing)
- 🔒 **Locked · room 7** — still sealed
- ⚠ **Trapped · room 6** — the one you left behind, now openable again

Fixed. You're right — Magic Missile fires **two** missiles, and the app was only firing one. It's been doing half its output every cast.

## What changed
- **Data:** Magic Missile now carries `missiles: 2`.
- **Casting:** `castCombatSpell` now loops once per missile:
  - **Two separate combat rolls**, each `d6 + Wil + H` vs the target's Defense, each dealing its Damage (1) on a hit — so up to **2 damage** total now instead of 1.
  - **Same or separate targets:** the first missile hits the monster you clicked; for the second, if more than one monster is standing you'll get a quick prompt to pick its target (defaults to the same one; Cancel keeps it on the same target). If only one monster's up, both just hit it automatically.
  - **AP cost stays 1** for the whole spell (both missiles), per the rules.
  - The log shows each shot: *"Magic Missile (missile 1/2): … HIT, 1 dmg"* then *"… (missile 2/2): …"*.

**Empower / Heighten interactions:** Heighten's doubled Hit applies to *both* missiles' rolls; Empower's bonus damage applies once (to the first missile), so it's not double-counted.

It's built generically off the `missiles` field, so any future multi-shot spell works the same way.

One thing I should flag: I only fixed it **going forward** — I can't cleanly reconstruct which past fights would've ended faster with the second missile, so I didn't try to retroactively compensate. ## How it works
A new **✨ Special Features** panel sits next to your Chests panel (visible from any room, even after you move on). Each feature shows its name, room, and **uses remaining**, with three buttons:

The Unstable Potion fudge is built (parses clean). Now to your general question.

## Short answer: two ways, depending on how automated you want it

**The key insight first:** in Pocket Dungeon a d6 roll only decides **hit or miss** — the *damage* is fixed by the weapon/spell, not the roll. So fudging a roll ±1 only ever changes anything when it pushes you *across* the hit/miss threshold. That makes fudging much simpler than it looks.

### 1. What exists right now (manual — works for any roll)
Open **Spend Fudge Points** (on the character sheet) → **"−1 FP: fudge a die roll (±1)"**. That spends the point and logs it, then you adjust the outcome by hand using the controls already on screen:
- Your attack *missed* and +1 would land it? Spend the point, then knock the target's HP down by its weapon/spell damage (the monster card's `−1` / dmg box).
- A monster *hit* you and −1 would make it miss? Spend the point, then bump your HP bar back up by the damage it dealt.
- It's deliberately a tracker + manual nudge, because the app resolves rolls instantly and there's no universal "undo."

### 2. What I'd build (automatic — for combat rolls)
A **"🎲 Fudge last roll (±1)"** button in the combat manager. After any attack/spell/monster-strike, it would let you spend 1 FP to bump *that* roll up or down:
- If the fudge flips **miss → hit**, it deals the damage automatically.
- If it flips **hit → miss**, it restores the HP (and un-kills the monster if it died).
- If the outcome doesn't change (still a hit or still a miss), it just notes the new roll and refunds nothing — so you'd only spend the point when it actually matters.

This is very doable precisely *because* rolls only decide hit/miss — I just track the last roll's threshold + target and re-check the flip. It's the clean general version of what I just built into the Unstable Potion.

Want me to build that "Fudge last roll" button? If so, should it cover **all** combat rolls (your attacks, your spells, *and* monster attacks on you), or just your own offense?

Also — relaunch to try the new Unstable Potion: quaffing it now pops a roll modal with **−1 / +1 (1 FP)** buttons so you can nudge it (e.g., a 6 down to a 5) before hitting **Keep**.

## How it works
Any weapon found at **Bonus Rating ≥ 1** shows a **`⚙ BR`** button (in inventory and on the equipped weapon). Clicking it opens an allocation modal where you spread that weapon's Bonus Rating across **Damage and/or Hit** — **1 BR per +1** to either, with `+1`/`−1` controls and a running "BR unspent" counter so you can't over-spend the budget. Save commits it to `brD`/`brH`.

Both bonuses are live in combat:
- **Damage** allocation adds to your hit damage (`D + brD`)
- **Hit** allocation adds to your attack roll (`H + brH`), making you land hits more often

And both show **blue** on the stat line — so a `D1+1 H1+1` split would highlight both.

## Your Wand
It's currently **D+2** (all 2 BR on Damage, the default). With the new button you can rebalance it — e.g. **D+1 / H+1** to land your wand attacks more reliably while still hitting a bit harder. Since you're a Willpower-based caster, the wand's attack roll is `d6 + Willpower + Hit`, so a point of Hit is a solid pickup if you're missing.

Both allocation modals (weapon and armor) cap spending at each item's locked **find-time** Bonus Rating, so nothing about the "no retroactive bonuses" rule changes — you're just re-splitting the points the item already earned.

## How it works
When you cast Fireball and it **hits** the target, the blast then deals the **same damage** to every other monster **in or adjacent to the target's square** — using the placed board tokens to figure out who's caught (same square, including stacked monsters, plus all 8 adjacent squares). - Splash damage matches the target's damage, including any Bonus Rating and Empower bonus.
- It resolves automatically **from your placed tokens**. If the target has no token placed, it hits just the target and pops a reminder to apply the splash by hand (since it can't know positions) — so place your monster tokens before lobbing a Fireball for the auto-resolution.
- Updated the spell's rulebook text to describe the blast.

One note on interpretation: you said "adjacent," and the rulebook data I had said "all monsters in that square" — I implemented the **union** (target's square *and* adjacent squares, diagonals included), so it covers both readings and behaves like a proper fireball. If your rulebook is stricter (only the *same* square, no adjacent), tell me and I'll tighten it to square-only.
